name: Carnitine Palmitoyltransferase I Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Biochemical Diagnostic Criteria for CPT I Deficiency

criteria.description: Episodes of hypoketotic hypoglycemia during fasting or illness
Elevated plasma free carnitine with low acylcarnitine species on tandem mass spectrometry
Identification of pathogenic variants in the CPT1A gene
Evidence of liver dysfunction or hepatomegaly during metabolic crises
Reduced CPT I enzyme activity in liver or fibroblast assays

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of hypoketotic hypoglycemia episodes plus either confirmatory biochemical profile or pathogenic CPT1A gene variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is considered the gold standard for definitive diagnosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic during fasting or metabolic stress

pathognomonic.symptomName: Elevated plasma free carnitine with low acylcarnitines
searchTerms: high free carnitine but low acylcarnitine
elevated plasma carnitine with low fatty acid carnitine

rare.notes: Muscle breakdown during prolonged fasting or illness

laboratory: Elevated plasma free carnitine with low long-chain acylcarnitines
imaging: Possible cardiomegaly on chest X-ray in severe cases
genetic: Pathogenic variants in CPT1A gene confirmed by molecular testing
other: Reduced CPT I enzyme activity in liver biopsy or cultured fibroblasts

distinguishingFeatures: CPT II deficiency typically presents with muscle symptoms and myoglobinuria
Normal or elevated ketones during hypoglycemia
MCAD deficiency shows elevated medium-chain acylcarnitines
More frequent episodes of hypoglycemia with ketosis

redFlags: Recurrent hypoketotic hypoglycemia during fasting or illness
Severe liver dysfunction or hepatomegaly in infancy
Sudden unexplained death in infancy or early childhood
references: Roe CR, et al. Carnitine palmitoyltransferase I deficiency: clinical, biochemical, and molecular studies. J Clin Invest. 1993.
Bonnefont JP, et al. Carnitine palmitoyltransferase deficiencies. Mol Genet Metab. 2004.
